newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM Dehaene not bidding for 3rd term - paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM Dehaene not bidding for 3rd term - paper.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene will not make a bid for a third term to the country's highest office, the De Standaard newspaper said on Monday.
"After two mandates, one has probably given the best one has. In one's own interest, it is best to stop then. But I have learned one does not always do what one wants," Dehaene told the newspaper.
"Next time I will pass on the baton, if it depends on me," he said.
Dehaene became prime minister in March 1992. He started his second term in June 1995.
In 1994 Dehaene narrowly lost a bid to become president of the European Commission (EU) because of a veto by British Prime Minister Johne Major, who considered him to be to pro-European.
Asked whether he still hoped to get the highest EU post, Dehaene said: "A chance like that you only get once in a lifetime. You create your own frustrations if you think you will get it again."
"I was not born in politics and I will not die in it," he said.
The current centre-left government's four-year term expires in 1999.
Christian-democrat Dehaene came to power via the christan-democratic labour movement.

Because of his union background, he is not seen as an ideal candidate to lead a possible centre-right government if the conservative liberals were to form a coalition with the christian-democrats after the next elections.
